title: Distortion bound from a controlled single-vector event
statement:
Let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, let $u, v \in \bbr^d$, and let $A$ be a real $k \times d$ matrix, acting as a linear map $\bbr^d \to \bbr^k$. Suppose the difference $u - v$ does not trigger the bad distortion event for $A$; that is, the squared-norm distortion of $u-v$ stays within the allowed band,
\[
  \bigl|\,\norm{A(u-v)}^2 - \norm{u-v}^2\,\bigr| \;\le\; \varepsilon\,\norm{u-v}^2 .
\]
Then the images $Au$ and $Av$ satisfy the two-sided single-pair distortion bound
\[
  (1 - \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 \;\le\; \norm{Au - Av}^2 \;\le\; (1 + \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 .
\]
hypotheses_covered: u, v are vectors in ℝ^d
A is a k×d real matrix (a linear map ℝ^d → ℝ^k)
u − v does not trigger the bad-single event: |‖A(u−v)‖² − ‖u−v‖²| ≤ ε‖u−v‖²
replaced:
If the matrix $A$ does \emph{not} trigger the bad-single event for the
difference $u - v$, then \texttt{JLDistortion} $\varepsilon\; u\; v\;
(A.toEuclideanLin\; u)\; (A.toEuclideanLin\; v)$ holds; that is, the
squared-distance of the images is within a factor of $(1 \pm \varepsilon)$
of the squared-distance of the originals.
